messages:
Lia (partnerships): quick Q — we keep hitting weird handoff cases when an SI brings a lead that spans cloud marketplace + HW partner bundles. want a short, operational rule + exceptions list. drafting below, pls flag holes.

Sanjay (eng-plat): +1. can we add a 'tech-fit' flag? if SI is running the POC / technical lead, they should own until POC acceptance or 2w no-response.

Alex (revops): +1 from revops. also need a canonical intake field `origin_channel` (si_marketplace, si_hw, direct_sales). that lets us dedupe and route. :eyes:

Matt (solutions): can you drop a couple of compact scenarios so we can test the rule?

Lia (partnerships): sure — rough table below (trying to keep it machine-friendly). please suggest fixes.

```csv
scenario,initial_owner,escalation_condition,escalate_to
SI submits lead via marketplace form,SI,if no contact in 14d,RevOps
SI brings HW-bundle + asks Redwood eval,Sales (named owner if exists),if technical scoping needed,Solutions
SI-originated joint-engagement where SI owns POC,SI,if SI requests handoff after POC,Sales/RevOps (per contract)
Marketplace lead with existing Redwood opportunity,RevOps,if conflicting owner in CRM,Partnerships + RevOps
Named account claimed by internal AE and also by SI,AE (CRM owner),if >30% pipeline overlap,Partnerships to mediate
```

Jena (sales): agree on the named account rule — CRM ownership should be the default tie-breaker unless there's a signed MSLA that says otherwise. also call out timing: if SI surfaces a competitive opportunity, AE has 72h to acknowledge or Partnerships steps in. :thumbsup:

Sanjay (eng-plat): tiny nuance — some HW vendors require tech co-signoff before sales can own SKU bundling. add exception: 'HW vendor contractual co-ownership -> require Solutions approval before AE takeover'.

Alex (revops): operational ask: i'll add `origin_channel` + `si_identifier` to intake form. can we standardize the escalation email to `partners+handoff@redwood.ai` so automation is simple?

Lia (partnerships): yes to standardized address. i'll push the decision tree as a 1-pager and a small flowchart in confluence tonight. will tag everyone for review.

Matt (solutions): example edge-case for testing — SI submits a PoC, SI signs an expense commitment for infra, AE also has an open renewal for the same account. Who sets price and who owns negotiations? my suggestion: commercial negotiation stays with AE if they initiated renewal; SI supports tech terms. escalate to Partnerships for split-commission if both claim.

Jena (sales): fwiw, commission split policy needs RevOps sign-off. we should link to partner comp policy in the playbook.

ops-bot: rule_created | key=handshake_edgecases_v1 | creator=Lia (partnerships) | ts=1737780150

Lia (partnerships): great feedback — next steps i captured: 1) Alex add intake fields (ETA: EOD tomorrow), 2) RevOps + Sales to confirm commission policy link (Jena/Alex), 3) Matt to bake the HW co-ownership clause into Solutions checklists, 4) i'll draft the 1-pager and attach flowchart. tagging follow-ups: @Alex (revops) @Matt (solutions) @Jena (sales).

Sanjay (eng-plat): sounds good. small ask: add a `requires_hw_coapproval` boolean to intake so infra teams see it upfront.

Alex (revops): noted — i'll include `requires_hw_coapproval` too. will bump process to automation once fields are live.

Lia (partnerships): thanks all — will update confluence and ping when PR is ready. :sparkles:
